Project brief

This project explores sensor-driven motor control using Arduino and ROS2. An ultrasonic distance sensor provides real-time input, which is used to control a Dynamixel motor and actuate a kinetic structure. A threshold-based control strategy with a buffer zone (hysteresis-like logic) is implemented to improve stability and avoid rapid switching. Key variables include distance (cm), threshold_close = 25 cm, threshold_open = 35 cm, threshold_stop = 60 cm, current_state (close / open / stop), and motor velocity commands. When the distance is less than 25 cm, the structure closes (Motor Velocity=+80); when between 35 cm and 60 cm, it opens(Motor Velocity=-80); and when above 60 cm, the motor stops(Motor Velocity=0). The buffer zone between 25 cm and 35 cm ensures smoother transitions.
